title: [Audit] 🔎 Elasticsearch Data Access
description: What data was read, by whom, through which transport action — including system indices.

config.description: All Elasticsearch audit events in range.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-elasticsearch" | STATS `Elasticsearch events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Distinct indices named in audited requests, with each data stream's backing indices and each run of dated daily indices counted once. Wildcard and date-math expressions (*, -*, <…{now/d}>) are patterns, not indices, and are left out.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | STATS BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE LOCATE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") == 0 AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE "<*" | EVAL family = REPLACE(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | STATS `Index families` = COUNT_DISTINCT(family)

config.description: Distinct Elasticsearch transport actions (cluster:*, indices:*), with shard-level copies and ES|QL sub-steps folded away — the same actions Top transport actions lists, all traffic.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action | WHERE NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") | STATS `Distinct actions` = COUNT(*)

config.description: ES|QL queries submitted — one per query, not per shard or sub-step. Includes the queries these dashboards run to draw themselves.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/esql" | STATS `ES|QL queries` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Requests touching dot-prefixed system and hidden indices (.kibana*, .security*, .slo-*, .alerts-*), counted once per index named. Backing indices of ordinary data streams (.ds-logs-…) are not system data and are left out, as are shard-level copies of a request.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | STATS `System index access` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Authorization denials. Sustained non-zero values mean a misconfigured client or a probe.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action == "access_denied" OR attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS `Access denied` = COUNT(*)

config.title: Data access over time by action family
config.description: Every Elasticsearch request that names a transport action, by kind of action — all traffic, the searches and ES|QL these dashboards run among the reads. Shard-level copies and ES|QL sub-steps are folded away so a request counts once, and authentication and connection events (which name no action) are left out, so it sums to less than the Elasticsearch events tile.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY time = BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action | WHERE NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") | EVAL family = CASE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read*", "read", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/write*", "write", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin*", "index admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin/xpack/security*", "security admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin*", "cluster admin", attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*:monitor*", "monitor", "other") | STATS events = SUM(n) BY time, family | SORT family

config.title: Who reads which index family
config.description: The 10 busiest identities across the top, and the 25 index families they read most down the side; a more solid cell is more requests, on a log scale. A data stream and its backing indices are one family, as is a run of dated daily indices; wildcard and date-math expressions are left out. A blank cell means that identity did not touch that family in range — or touched it too little to be among the 500 busiest identity/family pairs. A request naming several indices counts once per index. An identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id; one the audit names as such is labelled "· Cloud API key". Cells keep a heatmap's size when only a few identities or families are in range, so a sparse window draws a few cells, not solid blocks.

config.title: Top index families by events
config.description: The busiest index families, all traffic; the Index families tile counts every one, so the rest are beyond this list. How many distinct identities touch each is beside it. A data stream and its backing indices are one row, as is a run of dated daily indices; `Indices` says how many real indices the row folds together. Wildcard and date-math expressions are left out. A request naming several indices counts once per index.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE LOCATE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") == 0 AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE "<*" | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), index = REPLACE(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | STATS events = SUM(n), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices), actors = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor) BY index | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 14

config.title: Top transport actions
config.description: The busiest Elasticsearch transport actions with their request class, all traffic — the searches and ES|QL reads these dashboards run included, since reads are what this page is about. The Distinct actions tile counts every one; the rest are beyond this list. Shard-level copies and ES|QL sub-steps are folded away, so a request counts once. Identities is how many distinct identities sent the action; Request "—" means the event named no request class.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, request = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.request.name | WHERE NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), request = CASE(request IS NULL OR request == "", "—", request) | STATS events = SUM(n), actors = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor), last_seen = MAX(seen) BY attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, request | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: Denied requests · none is good
config.description: Who was refused, what they asked for and on which index — newest first, the most recent of what the Access denied tile counts. Index "—" is a cluster-level request; <anonymous> with action "—" is an HTTP call that carried no credentials. A request naming several indices shows once per index. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action == "access_denied" OR attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, index = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), index = COALESCE(index, "—"), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action = COALESCE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, "—") | KEEP actor, index, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action, events, last_seen | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 7

config.title: ⚠️ Who touched system and hidden indices · often empty at 1h
config.description: Who touched system and hidden indices — Kibana internals, the security index, alerting and SLO data — one row per identity, index group (.alerts*, .slo*, .kibana*…) and action. `Indices` says how many real indices the row covers; the Discover session below names each one. Sorted by most recent, not by volume: sorting by volume buries a one-off read under routine polling. Backing indices of ordinary data streams (.ds-logs-…) and shard-level copies of a request are left out. Expected from Kibana and platform automation; unexpected from anyone else. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, action = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), area = CONCAT(REPLACE(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.[^-._]+).*$""", "$1"), "*") | STATS events = SUM(n), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.elasticsearch.audit.indices), last_seen = MAX(seen) BY actor, area, action | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: System index requests, newest 1,000 (raw) · often empty at 1h
config.description: The raw events behind the table above: the newest 1,000 requests against a system or hidden index, one row per index named, newest first. It stops at 1,000, so it can hold fewer rows than the System index access tile counts — the "1,000 results" above the grid is that cap, not the total. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.
